text: Confirm the threshold logic in DiscountPolicy.discountRate: subtotalCents >= 10_000 triggers a 10% discount for REGULAR customers (VIP always gets 20%, so use REGULAR tier orders for these tests).

In /src/test/java/com/sweforge/pricing/PricingCalculatorTest.java, add a @Test method for subtotal 9,999 cents (single Item(9_999)) asserting the total equals 9,999 (no discount, since 9,999 < 10,000).
Add a @Test method for subtotal exactly 10,000 cents (single Item(10_000)) asserting the total equals 9,000 (10% discount applied at the boundary, since 10,000 >= 10,000).
Add a @Test method for subtotal 10,001 cents (single Item(10_001)) asserting the total equals 9,001 rounded per Math.round(10_001 * 0.90) = 9,001 (10% discount applied above the boundary).

Follow existing test conventions: use the shared 'calculator' field, List.of(...) for items, default REGULAR tier via the single-arg Order constructor, and assertEquals(expected, actual) formatting consistent with existing tests.
Do not modify DiscountPolicy.java, PricingCalculator.java, or any other production source file — this is a test-only change.

Run the focused test class (e.g., mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test) under Java 21 to verify the three new boundary tests and existing tests pass, then run the full 'mvn test' suite as a final validation per the pricing-build-validation skill.
